hominibus in Graecia natis favet quia Hellas atque Ionia Virgini subiacent secun-
dum Pauli Alexandrini doctrinam; cf. Bouché-Leclercq, Astrol. grecque, p. 330.
sections.en:
¹ Spica of the celestial Virgin makes priestesses of the goddesses who give the fruits of the earth, and
favors men born in Greece because Hellas and Ionia lie under the Virgin accord-
ing to the doctrine of Paulus Alexandrinus; cf. Bouché-Leclercq, Astrol. grecque, p. 330.

summary.headline: Astrological Effects of Bright Stars
summary.text: Astrological delineations of Ares, Aphrodite, Kronos, Zeus, and the five bright stars in nativities, including sexual temperament, fertility, medicine, prophecy, priesthood, honors, kingship, and physical fame. Spica, Crown, Fish, the Lion’s heart, Arcturus, Arctophylax, and the Eagle are located by zodiacal degrees, with a footnote linking Spica’s effects in Greece to Paulus Alexandrinus and Bouché-Leclercq.
